R101.note: Rejects any object/array value in extraCriteria, blocking Mongo operator injection while preserving scalar narrowing.

R102.note: Alnum/hyphen/underscore allowlist on pluginName correctly prevents traversal in the dynamic require path.

R103.note: GET->POST plus ValidateAntiForgeryToken with an updated form is the correct, fully disclosed fix.

R104.note: Moves param into the JNDI filterArgs placeholder so DirContext.search escapes it per RFC 4515; preserves original filter shape.

R105.note: snprintf with explicit size checks replaces strcpy/strcat, preserving the function's signature and success-path output.

R106.note: Standard mysqli prepared statement with bind_param; return shape unchanged.

R107.note: Allowlist validates the ORDER BY column name against known columns with a disclosed safe default for invalid input.

R108.note: Extension is derived from the already-detected MIME type instead of the client-supplied name, closing the mismatch.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES on both fields is the correct, complete fix.

R110.note: Bounds check before the array write is the appropriate, minimal fix.

R111.note: sendmail() plus an explicit CRLF-rejecting regex closes the envelope-injection vector; version claim about putcmd() CRLF rejection is accurate.

R112.note: ANY($1) parameterization correctly closes injection, but the added Number.isInteger requirement is stricter than needed and would silently reject legitimate numeric-string ids without saying so.

R113.note: True-extension check plus a randomized filename fully closes the double-extension bypass; the filename change is stated plainly.

R114.note: resize(count) replaces reserve(count), preserving exact element values and final size.

R115.note: Correct self-invocation fix pattern, but adding @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") to the method the code's own comment calls the 'Nightly batch job entry point' will silently break that scheduled job, since it has no authenticated SecurityContext; not mentioned.

R116.note: Callback form of setTimeout eliminates the eval-like string path entirely, cleanest possible fix.

R117.note: res.sendFile with { root } is the documented, idiomatic Express containment mechanism.

R118.note: Correct signature-verification approach, but the sample uses `new Key(...)` without `use Firebase\JWT\Key;`, so it fatals as literally written.

R119.note: Secure = true is the direct, correct fix.

R120.note: execFile with an argument array removes shell interpretation of domain; residual single-token flag-injection risk is minimal since the value isn't split into separate argv entries.

R121.note: require_http_methods(["POST"]) plus csrf_protect and an updated form matches exactly what the case's own settings.py comment calls for.

R122.note: Building the instance and calling full_clean() before save() correctly triggers the bypassed field validator.

R123.note: No working verification code is given (VerifyAssemblySignature and trustedPublicKeyToken are undefined placeholders), and strong-name verification is not a reliable mechanism on modern .NET, so it's unclear the vector actually closes or that legitimate plugins would still load.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) is the correct, minimal DRF ownership binding.

R125.note: Replaces eval with ast.literal_eval/numexpr, avoiding the __builtins__ sandbox-escape shown; the literal_eval attempt is effectively dead code for formulas with variables but is harmless since it falls through.

R126.note: AES-256 with a random IV and PKCS7 padding correctly replaces DES; the weak string-to-key derivation is explicitly flagged as a production follow-up, matching the original code's equally weak key handling.

R127.note: finfo_file() magic-byte detection plus a randomized filename fully closes the double-extension bypass; the filename change is disclosed.

R128.note: %255s bounds the write into nameBuf, but 255 still exceeds line's real 64-byte allocation, so sscanf can still read up to 255 bytes past line's buffer looking for a delimiter - the reported OOB read is only shrunk, not eliminated.

R129.note: Rejects path separators/dot components in the filename before concatenation, correctly replacing the broken realpath-on-nonexistent-file pattern the code comments themselves describe.

R130.note: Swapping {!! !!} for {{ }} enables Blade's auto-escaping, the correct fix.

R131.note: Host check only runs when uri.isAbsolute() is true, but a scheme-relative URL like "//evil.com/path" has no scheme (isAbsolute()==false) so it skips the check and still redirects off-site - a well-known open-redirect bypass left open.

R132.note: lockoutOnFailure: true is the direct, correct fix.

R133.note: escapeshellarg() on both interpolated values closes the shell injection and matches the safe pattern already used elsewhere in the same file.

R134.note: Escaping backticks and quotes blocks statement-separator style injection, but never escapes '$', so PowerShell subexpression injection via $(...) inside the double-quoted value still executes arbitrary commands.

R135.note: Rejects absolute paths (which Path.resolve() would otherwise let bypass the base) and uses toRealPath() plus a startsWith containment check; appropriate since this is a read of an existing file, not a write of a new one.

R136.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) is the correct CSPRNG-backed replacement for uniqid().

R137.note: Parameterized LIKE query correctly closes injection, but introduces an undisclosed 255-character parameter size that could truncate or error on longer legitimate search terms that worked before.

R138.note: html.EscapeString() on both interpolated fields before Sprintf is a correct, complete fix.

R139.note: Generic client-facing message with server-side logging is the correct, disclosed fix.

R140.note: escape-html on the interpolated query value is a correct, complete fix.
